lead: Apple's HomeView hardware sits boxed in warehouses waiting on its assistant; HybridAgents think in latent space but act in text; Schwab's CEO doubts sleep-trading agents; and Europe's industrials cash in on the build-out on diverging bets.

sections.title: Apple's HomeView: boxed hardware, missing software
sections.intro: Gurman says finished HomeView units have sat in warehouses for the better part of a year while the assistant software lagged - and Gruber revisits a bad prediction about its design.

sections.title: Agents that reason beyond text
sections.intro: A new architecture mixes latent-space thinking with text-based tool use, claiming better performance at a fraction of the tokens.

sections.title: Agents meet real money and real voters
sections.intro: Charles Schwab's CEO doubts autonomous stock-trading agents, while a prediction market sets a concrete bar for an AI-clone presidential candidate in 2028.

sections.title: AI infrastructure's valuation test
sections.intro: Europe's industrial giants split on software vs. equipment as AI demand lifts both, and Nscale's ~$30B IPO target meets investor resistance.

sections.title: Community norms and developer tooling
sections.intro: Lobsters bans bare repo links after a wave of AI-era low-effort posts, an engineer makes the case for running your own LLM proxy, and small releases polish the LLM plugin ecosystem.

sections.title: Agents reach personal messaging
sections.intro: A self-hosted MCP server gives AI agents read-only access to your WhatsApp chats, with the phone staying the source of truth.

sections.title: Etcetera
sections.intro: A subscription drive for an independent comic strip, funded directly by readers.

sections.title: Model frontier: DeepSeek's fast, verbose open weight
sections.intro: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 lands near the top of the Artificial Analysis index at a moderate price - if you can afford its verbosity.

sections.title: Agents start spending: Stripe's first real numbers
sections.intro: Stripe Link data shows agent-driven transactions up 38x in September, while Sam Altman's World pitches banks on verifying both humans and agents.

sections.title: AI's macro footprint: exports, jobs and the G20
sections.intro: AI-driven exports lift China's Q3 GDP, US cybersecurity hiring rotates toward AI roles, and economists expect the gains to spread - unevenly.

sections.title: Compute for inference: Intel's 480GB bet
sections.intro: Intel's D-series trades bandwidth for capacity with LPDDR5X, aiming at running huge models rather than training them.

sections.title: Forecasting and trust under stress
sections.intro: A historic El Nino will test whether AI weather models deserve the decisions already riding on them.

sections.title: Applied AI: caregivers and research assistants
sections.intro: Abby Care raises $82M to make family members certified paid caregivers, and a Show HN tries the Codex pattern for science.

sections.title: Workflows and culture
sections.intro: tmux becomes the agent operations layer, Troy Hunt builds HIBP AI-first as 'vibe coding' goes mainstream, and Doctorow argues surveillance - not advertising - is the internet's original sin.

sections.title: Trusting the code agents write
sections.intro: A Meta engineer's black-box discomfort, a practitioner's pyramid for trusting agents, and a fine-tune that scrubs AI writing tics.

sections.title: The harness is the body
sections.intro: A free book builds agents from first principles around the loop that owns the context.

sections.title: Agents as insider threats
sections.intro: Microsoft ships agent risk monitoring in 365 E7 as a $5,000 token budget fuels a 1,200-site hacking campaign.

sections.title: Model moves: Aurora leaks, Replit defects, DeepSeek adds web tools
sections.intro: Three mystery image models hit the arena, Replit drops Anthropic for OpenAI, and DeepSeek gives agents Search and Fetch APIs.

sections.title: Silicon for the agent era
sections.intro: Nvidia's Vera team says agents reverse CPU design priorities, Qualcomm hears labs want 100B models on phones by 2028, and Tenstorrent banks $1.5B.

sections.title: Playing and governing
sections.intro: Four Gemini agents beat Minecraft on their own, while Democrats eye committee power over the industry and Pew maps a closing gender gap.

sections.title: Deals and their structures
sections.intro: Character.AI's bankruptcy as a Disney deal mechanism, Anthropic's opaque trust, Musk's $10.5B pledge, and an agent Q&A plugin that tripled signups.

sections.title: Thompson's question: do you trust Apple?
sections.intro: Stratechery contrasts the 1999 AirPort keynote with the HomeView saga and asks what Cook's Apple optimized away.

sections.title: China's stack closes ranks; Washington pushes back
sections.intro: DeepSeek and Huawei co-design chips and plan Ascend pre-training, while DHS orders DeepSeek out of federal systems.

sections.title: The build-out's next contracts
sections.intro: Nscale talks a ~$45B Anthropic deal days after its IPO valuation wobbled, and Nvidia's Vera CPU wins Modal for agent hosting.

sections.title: New models: MiniMax's leap and a diffusion bet
sections.intro: MiniMax M3.1 Flash claims a generational jump with weights due Thursday, and Inception Labs takes diffusion to scale.

sections.title: CUDA's challengers get practical
sections.intro: Amazon's TorchNeuron runs PyTorch on Trainium with no rewrites, while doubleAI's Maxwell optimizes code as it executes.

sections.title: AI proves a theorem, and a field wobbles
sections.intro: An AI proves the quasi-Riemann hypothesis; Berkeley's math community faces the crossroads.

sections.title: Consumer AI, two ways
sections.intro: Tolan raises $30M serving non-technical users (70% women), while tinkerers aim Claude Code at their smart TVs.

sections.title: Money and tooling around agents
sections.intro: Town hits a $1B valuation, CERN partners with Mistral, Laminar watches agent traces, and the ecosystem fills in with benches, databases and small apps.

sections.title: Built for someone specific
sections.intro: A phonics reader for a six-year-old and a task app built to end drudgery.

sections.title: Mercury 3 makes the diffusion case
sections.intro: Inception's new diffusion LLM claims Luna/Haiku quality at 1,000 tokens a second - and it used agent swarms to speed itself up another 16%.

sections.title: AI for science and for math
sections.intro: CERN partners with Mistral on foundation models for discovery, while Berkeley mathematicians reckon with the quasi-Riemann proof.

sections.title: Inside an AI-run intrusion campaign
sections.intro: Cairn publishes the actual tasking documents of agent-driven cyber operations - target lists, objectives, payloads and all.

sections.title: The cap-table carousel
sections.intro: Eric Schmidt holds ~1% of Anthropic, OpenAI races to lock commitments before Anthropic's IPO, and Town's assistants hit unicorn status.

sections.title: The labor question, in two registers
sections.intro: An obituary for programming's puzzle-solving joy, and the team that beat the APIs with a 235B fine-tune and shipped nothing.

sections.title: Tools people actually reach for
sections.intro: A phonics reader built for one six-year-old, a three-task app, KiviDB's 21M GETs a second, and Tolan's companion for non-tech users.

sections.title: Chips without clusters
sections.intro: Skymizer claims 700B inference on one 240W card while Amazon's TorchNeuron erases the PyTorch-to-Trainium rewrite.

sections.title: Culture and community friction
sections.intro: A decompilation site closes over AI contributions, HN asks again for dark mode, and Westenberg on why normal people still laugh.

sections.title: Watching the agents
sections.intro: 'Superfan' Claudes each guarding one component, and Laminar's RL model that finds errors in every trace.

sections.title: Sites fight back against assistants
sections.intro: WhatsApp's hidden help-page instructions told AI not to point users to the regulator - prompt injection as product policy.

sections.title: Robots and new launchpads
sections.intro: Dream Labs APIs its robot foundation model, Vortex Code ships teams from a prompt, MiniMax details M3.1 Flash, and TVs get de-bloated by agents.

sections.title: Agents as weapons
sections.intro: Leaked documents show Army Cyber Command's ECHOTRIBBLE: agents built to spread through networks and neutralize targets.

sections.title: DeepSeek's federal ban, confirmed
sections.intro: Reuters and the Federal Register put the DHS order on the record.

sections.title: Running agents well
sections.intro: A factory boilerplate that cut token spend 80%, and the intelligence-versus-tools trade-off users keep hitting.

sections.title: The solo operator's contingency plan
sections.intro: A self-hosted dead man's switch that tells the right people in the right order.
